findings.title: Avoid crash when Google Meet is selected and no destination calendar exists
Restore the slug condition for organization creation
Restore the fallback to the destination calendar in Google update/delete
Google createEvent ignores destination calendars without a credentialId
Other calendar providers always use the main host's calendar for every host's credential

response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Avoid crash when Google Meet is selected and no destination calendar exists

Affected:
- packages/core/EventManager.ts:117-119

Explanation:
`mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]`. Many callers in this PR now pass `[]` or `null`.

Before this change, `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` safely evaluated to `undefined`, and the code fell back to Cal Video. Now, if the location is Google Meet, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a `TypeError`, so `create()` fails and the booking fails.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];
if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar") {
  evt["location"] = "integrations:daily";
}
~~~

## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Restore the slug condition for organization creation

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151

Explanation:
The original code set `slug` only when billing is **disabled**: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`. The rewrite sets it only when billing is **enabled**, which flips the behavior.

The result:
- With billing enabled, the slug is assigned immediately, before payment or verification. It also duplicates `requestedSlug`.
- With billing disabled, organizations are created with no slug.

This change is also unrelated to the PR's purpose.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}),
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Restore the fallback to the destination calendar in Google update/delete

Affected:
- packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254-256
- packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-317

Explanation:
The fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. In that branch, `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares each entry against that same falsy value, so it effectively always returns `undefined`.

Previously the code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Now:
- `update` sends `calendarId: undefined`, which fails the API call.
- `delete` targets `primary` even when the event lives in another calendar.

This hits legacy references that have no `externalCalendarId`.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId || mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;
~~~

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Google createEvent ignores destination calendars without a credentialId

Affected:
- packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147-154

Explanation:
`selectedCalendar` is now found only by matching `credentialId`. Destination calendars with a null `credentialId` are legacy records, handled by the `else` branch in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`. For those, no match is found, so the event is created in `primary` instead of the user's chosen calendar.

Before this change, `destinationCalendar.externalId` was used directly. Fall back to the first entry whose `credentialId` is unset.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const selectedCalendar =
  calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId ??
  calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => !cal.credentialId)?.externalId;
~~~

## 5) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Other calendar providers always use the main host's calendar for every host's credential

Affected:
- packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73-77
- packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-165
- packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128-129

Explanation:
`EventManager` now calls `createEvent` once per collective host, each time with that host's credential. However, Office365, CalDAV (base service) and Lark always pick `destinationCalendar[0]`, which is the main host's calendar.

The effect for a non-main host's credential:
- **Office365:** it targets a calendar id that host doesn't own, which gives a 404 or the wrong calendar.
- **CalDAV:** the `filter` matches nothing, so no event is created.
- **Lark:** it uses the wrong calendar.

Use the `credentialId` now passed to `createEvent` to pick the matching destination, as the Google implementation does.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number) {
  const destination =
    event.destinationCalendar?.find((c) => c.credentialId === credentialId) ??
    event.destinationCalendar?.[0];
  ...
}
~~~

## 6) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Team hosts' calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar

Affected:
- packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1079

Explanation:
`evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that case, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently does nothing.

As a result, the collective hosts' destination calendars are ignored. This is the exact scenario the PR is meant to fix.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar
  ? [eventType.destinationCalendar]
  : organizerUser.destinationCalendar
  ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar]
  : [],
...
if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") {
  evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars];
}
~~~

## 7) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Video/conferencing references lose their credentialId

Affected:
- packages/core/EventManager.ts:169-170

Explanation:
Previously, non-calendar results stored `credentialId: result.credentialId`. Now non-calendar results (video apps such as Zoom or Daily) get `credentialId: undefined`.

Later update/delete paths that look up the video credential by `reference.credentialId` will no longer find it. Only calendar references should change.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined,
credentialId: result.credentialId,
~~~

## 8) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Dynamic users no longer select organization

Affected:
- packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:731-740

Explanation:
The refactor of `loadUsers` removed `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-user query. Downstream code that reads `organizerUser.organization?.slug` (for example, booker URL generation) will silently get `undefined` for dynamic group bookings.

The change also alters error handling:
- An empty `dynamicUserList` now becomes a generic 500 instead of the previous behavior.
- Any `HttpError` (e.g. a 404) is rewritten to 400.

This depends on code outside the diff, which is why the severity is MEDIUM.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
select: {
  ...userSelect.select,
  credentials: true,
  metadata: true,
  organization: { select: { slug: true } },
},
~~~
Rethrow an `HttpError` unchanged instead of converting it to a 400.

## 9) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Recurring cancellation repeats deletes once per reference and ignores other hosts

Affected:
- packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:422-470

Explanation:
The recurring branch is now inside the per-reference loop. For every calendar reference it:
- iterates over all of the organizer's calendar credentials, and
- deletes the first calendar reference of every updated booking.

With N host references, the same events are deleted N times. That produces 404/410 errors and wasted API calls. Other hosts' events in recurring bookings are never deleted, because `updBooking.references.find` only takes the first reference and only the organizer's credentials are used.

Run the recurring branch once outside the loop. Within it, iterate over each booking's references and use each reference's own credential.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
if (isRecurringCancelAll) {
  for (const updBooking of updatedBookings) {
    for (const ref of updBooking.references.filter((r) => r.type.includes("_calendar"))) {
      const cred = await resolveCredential(ref.credentialId);
      const cal = cred && (await getCalendar(cred));
      apiDeletes.push(cal?.deleteEvent(ref.uid, evt, ref.externalCalendarId));
    }
  }
} else { /* per-reference loop */ }
~~~

## 10) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: updateEvent may be called with an undefined credential

Affected:
- packages/core/EventManager.ts:511-542

Explanation:
If the credential is neither in `this.calendarCredentials` nor in the DB (or has no app slug), `credential` stays `undefined`. It is still passed to `updateEvent`, which will throw or behave unpredictably.

Also, `credential` is declared outside the loop, so a value from a previous iteration could leak into the next one.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
let credential = this.calendarCredentials.find((c) => c.id === reference.credentialId);
...
if (credential) result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId));
~~~

## 11) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Restore logging of update failures

Affected:
- packages/core/EventManager.ts:593-608

Explanation:
`console.error(message)` was removed from the catch block, so failures while updating calendar events are now swallowed silently. Restore logging, preferably with the project logger.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
log.error(message);
~~~

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate: mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined when evt.destinationCalendar is null or [], causing TypeError crash when location is Google Meet instead of falling back to Cal Video
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: mainHostDestinationCalendar being undefined when evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array. Both point to the same null reference/destructuring issue in the Google Calendar service. The candidate adds context about the TypeError crash and Google Meet location, but the core issue identified is identical.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate: Organization creation slug condition is inverted - slug is now set when billing is enabled instead of disabled, causing slug assignment before payment/verification and missing slugs when billing is disabled
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment - the logic inversion in organization creation where the slug property is now set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true instead of when it's false. The candidate correctly notes this causes slug assignment before payment/verification when billing is enabled, and missing slugs when billing is disabled. This is the same underlying bug about the inverted condition.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate: updateEvent may be called with undefined credential if not found in calendarCredentials or DB, and credential declared outside loop may leak between iterations
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same core problem as the golden comment - that `updateEvent` may be called with an undefined credential when the credential is not found. The candidate mentions both the calendarCredentials lookup and DB lookup scenarios, which aligns with the golden comment's concern about `reference.credentialId` being set but the credential not being found. Both issues point to the same potential runtime error from passing undefined credential to updateEvent.

false_positives.candidate: Google calendar update/delete fallback branch compares against falsy externalCalendarId, causing update to send undefined calendarId and delete to target primary instead of correct calendar for legacy references

Google createEvent ignores destination calendars without credentialId - legacy records with null credentialId are not matched, causing events to be created in primary instead of user's chosen calendar
Office365, CalDAV and Lark calendar providers always use destinationCalendar[0] (main host's calendar) for every host's credential, causing 404 errors or wrong calendar for non-main hosts
Team hosts' calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar because push on null silently does nothing
Video/conferencing references lose their credentialId - non-calendar results now get undefined credentialId, breaking later update/delete paths that look up video credential by reference.credentialId
Dynamic users query no longer selects organization slug, causing undefined for organizerUser.organization?.slug in dynamic group bookings
Dynamic users error handling changed - empty dynamicUserList becomes generic 500 and HttpError is rewritten to 400
Recurring cancellation is inside per-reference loop, causing same events to be deleted N times and other hosts' events in recurring bookings to never be deleted
Logging of calendar update failures was removed, causing failures to be swallowed silently

false_negatives.golden_comment: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
